purpose: First static comparison supporting a Cobalt-free Xiaomi source-normalization investigation. This is evidence for what to test live, not a rendering replacement decision.
sourceCamera: Xiaomi 15 Ultra rear wide/main RAW camera

nativeEvidence.source: 12 Open Camera DNGs from the fixed M9 regression/capture corpus
nativeEvidence.stability: ColorMatrix1/2, CameraCalibration1/2 and ForwardMatrix1/2 were identical across all 12 inspected DNGs; AsShotNeutral varied by scene

currentEmbeddedCobaltEvidence.profileSource: Xiaomi 15 Ultra Rear Wide Camera Cobalt Modular.dcp

matrixDifferenceDiagnostics.note: Frobenius distances are descriptive only. They do not measure visual error and do not include the Cobalt HueSatMap.

interpretation: Xiaomi exposes a stable dual-illuminant native characterization for the main RAW camera, so Cobalt is not required merely to obtain a defined sensor transform.
The native and Cobalt matrix sets are materially different numerically; therefore removing Cobalt must be an A/B colour-science experiment, not a blind substitution.
Cobalt also contributes a dual-illuminant 90x30 HueSatMap. Matrix parity alone cannot establish that native Camera2 metadata reproduces the same hue behaviour.
The Leica M9 target should remain defined separately from either Xiaomi source characterization.
nextEvidence: Collect SOURCECAL1A + RAWSHADING1A live sidecars from all four Xiaomi rear physical cameras.
Confirm complete native ColorMatrix/ForwardMatrix/CalibrationTransform metadata per physical camera.
Construct a render A/B for the main camera: existing Cobalt adapter versus native Camera2 sensor-to-XYZ, with all M9 firmware target stages frozen.
If native-only hue errors remain, solve a small empirical source correction per Xiaomi sensor rather than embedding Leica target colour into the source adapter.
